services.name: Lane rental
services.desc: Located only minutes from BIMA, Daisy Lane will be centered on a large, newly renovated, light-filled space where artists can create and explore in a focused environment while BIMA’s community can interact with the artists during the creation of new work. The central program at Daisy Lane will be a year-round artist residency for artists working in book arts, letterpress, screenprinting, Risograph, and other related art forms. The space will also be an active location for youth engagement, BIMA’s Open Book Tours events, workshops, art events, and lectures. services.name: Summer Camps
services.desc: Each experience gives kids aged 6-11 the space to explore their creativity, learn, make friends, and find inspiration within themselves. Our camps are led by certificated teaching artists and are designed around different themes, making each week fun and memorable! As a thank you for your continued support, current BIMA Members receive 10% off the cost of summer camp tuition and access to early registration. Become a member today and see all the ways you can benefit from supporting the arts! Each year, BIMA allocates resources to make it possible for students who love art to take part in our Summer Camps. services.name: Rental Events
services.desc: Music inspired by the roads traveled, the relationships formed, and the cultures carried along the way will move you during Jun Iida’s “Bellflower” program! Three years ago, trumpeter and composer Jun Iida left Seattle for New York, and this program, built with a band of new friends over the course of a West Coast tour, is the sound of that journey. “Bellflower” is mostly original music, drawn directly from Iida’s own experience moving between places, people, and identities. It’s a program shaped by Japanese heritage, American cities, and the particular restlessness of starting over somewhere new.
